name: Zerubbabel
overview: Zerubbabel is a male figure noted for his place in the lineage of the Messiah, as recorded in Luke 3:27. While his tribal affiliation is not specified, his significance is tied to his genealogical role in the fulfillment of God's redemptive plan. There are no additional notes provided about his character or life.
namesAndTitles: The name Zerubbabel means 'offspring [seed] of Babylon; scion i.e., one grafted into the [plant of] Babylon,' highlighting his connection to the Babylonian exile context. This proper name, as given in Luke 3:27, reflects his historical and spiritual heritage but was not directly given by God.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture identifies Rhesa as Zerubbabel's father, an inferred relationship, and Shealtiel as his son, an explicit relationship, both noted in Luke 3:27. Beyond these, no further family relationships are recorded.
scriptureSignificance: Zerubbabel's primary biblical importance lies in his role within the messianic genealogy, linking the line of Christ through a post-exilic context. His presence in Luke's genealogy underscores God's faithfulness in preserving the messianic line despite the Babylonian captivity. This connection emphasizes the continuity of God's redemptive promises culminating in Jesus Christ.
